title: Request fingerprint routing and smoothed prefetch protocol for dashboard queries
creator: Tomás Herrera
description: Reduce 99th percentile latency for dashboard paginated queries by combining a lightweight request fingerprint routing layer with a smoothed prefetch protocol and compact index summarizer. Goal is to keep interactive dashboards responsive under multi-tenant load while avoiding read amplification and uncontrolled cache churn.
acceptance_criteria: P99 tail latency for common dashboard endpoints reduced by >=25% under synthetic mixed workload compared to baseline
No more than 10% increase in read amplification (IO ops) vs baseline when smoothed prefetch is enabled
Feature gated behind runtime flag and configurable per-tenant policy (enabled/disabled, aggressiveness) in Console
End-to-end integration tests covering cache priming, cache miss fallthrough, and fallback hedging added to CI
Relevant dashboards show clear per-route token/read cost delta and new metrics (fingerprint-hit-rate, smoothed-prefetch-ops)
design_decisions: Use short (64-bit) request fingerprints derived from route + query signature + tenant id to route similar reads to the same prefetch worker, minimizing KV cache contention
Implement smoothed prefetch as a leaky-bucket that issues prefetches at a controlled rate per-tenant to avoid thundering herds. Prefetch aggressiveness parameterized (alpha in [0.0, 1.0]).
Maintain a compact index summarizer (min-sketch + short bloom) per time-window to decide whether a prefetch is likely to hit, avoiding wasteful IO on cold indexes
Favor read-through microcache for small hot ranges with LRU+frequency boosting; larger sweeps use a background async materializer with backpressure
Fallback hedging policy: if prefetch hasn't returned in X ms and request is tail-bound, issue a hedged read to alternative shard or smaller projection to preserve latency SLO
Expose metrics and trace points for fingerprint distribution, prefetch queue depth, prefetch latency percentiles, and eviction churn to enable postrollout tuning
implementation_notes: Server-side: add fingerprinting middleware in query-router service; fingerprint encoded as base64 8-byte string and propagated in request headers
Prefetch worker: new service 'prefetch-agent' written in Go, subscribes to route groups and tenant buckets via kinesis stream for workload locality
Index summarizer: run periodic compaction job producing per-route bloom/minsketch artifacts stored in metadata store (S3) with version pins
Console backend: add feature flag and per-route controls in rollout service (canary -> A/B -> global), integrate rollout metrics into Console
Testing: synthetic harness (k6) with tenant skews and hotspot scenarios; replay real production traces for representative tail behavior
DB changes: add compact prefetch_metadata table with TTL and eviction policy; avoid table scans on warm paths by using prefix keys
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff - scoped feature to 3 high-traffic dashboard routes and one low-latency tenant as pilot. Benchmarks defined.
2026-03-11: Prototype fingerprint middleware implemented and validated for collision rate (<1e-7) in unit tests. Initial routing to existing prefetch queue works.
2026-03-12: Index summarizer PoC (bloom + min-sketch) produced artifacts with 7% false-positive at target size. Prefetch leaky-bucket basic implementation completed; needs tuning under load.
2026-03-12: Integration smoke test showed 18% P99 improvement on pilot routes with conservative prefetch alpha=0.2. Observed one tenant with high eviction churn — added to watchlist.
notes_risks: Risk: mis-tuned prefetch can increase IO costs and evict genuinely hot entries; mitigated with conservative default and per-tenant caps
Risk: fingerprint collisions could route dissimilar queries together; chosen 64-bit fingerprint has acceptable collision risk but monitors must alert if distribution skews
Operational complexity: new background workers add failure domains; include healthchecks and automated restart policies and runbooks
Data correctness: ensure prefetched projections are strongly consistent with read path; avoid stale results by using short TTLs and versioned prefetched artifacts
next_steps: A: Add integration test that replays a 24h production trace with prefetch enabled and measure read amplification
B: Instrument detailed metrics and alerts for prefetch cost delta and eviction churn; baseline current cost before large-scale rollout
C: Run pilot on 3 tenants for two weeks with gradual canary ramp; capture customer-facing latency and cost telemetry
D: Complete PR for prefetch-agent and design doc updates, then request design review from infra and SRE teams
